_comment: SD-LEO-INFRA-CLOSE-REMAINING-SECURITY-001 FR-6. Functions exempted from secdef-execute-revoke-lint.mjs, each with a mandatory non-empty reason. Add an entry only when a SECURITY DEFINER function genuinely does not need a same-file REVOKE (e.g. it's intentionally PUBLIC-callable by design, documented and reviewed) -- do not use this to silence a real gap.

ventures_canonical_writer_policy.reason: SD-LEO-INFRA-STAGE-WRITER-CHOKE-001: this function (database/chairman-gated/20260825_ventures_canonical_writer_choke.sql) is LANGUAGE sql, no SECURITY DEFINER modifier -- SECURITY INVOKER by default. It is not actually a SECURITY DEFINER function; the lint's bounded look-ahead window matched the literal text 'SECURITY DEFINER RPC' appearing inside this function's OWN returned VALUES data -- descriptive notes strings documenting the security posture of OTHER registered functions (advance_venture_stage etc.), not a clause on this function itself. Even setting the false-positive aside: this function's real PUBLIC-grant closure is intentionally split into a SEPARATE, later-ordered file (20260825_ventures_canonical_writer_policy_revoke.sql, step 4 of 4) rather than an inline same-file REVOKE, because the REVOKE cannot apply until the function exists (step 3) -- the exact ceremony-ordering convention this directory's README documents, and the same split R5's sd_canonical_writer_policy entry (below) already uses for its own registry function.
